newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives seek to widen personal investment.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives seek to widen personal investment.

text.p: Britain's Conservative Party will continue to explore ways to use the tax system to encourage personal savings.
In its election manifesto, released on Wednesday, the party said it will look to develop existing tax exemptions for savings to allow people to secure their futures more effectively.
It will also strive to widen share ownership among the population at large.
"Our goal is that by 2000, more than half of the employees of Britain's largest companies will own shares in those companies," the manifesto said.
It said 4.5 million people already benefit from tax-exempt savings schemes, known as TESSAs, and another 2.5 million have personal equity plans -- PEPs.
"We will continue to build on this success," the party pledged in its manifesto.
In order for life savings not to be eroded too much, a Conservative government would continue to raise the threshold for inheritance tax "as it is prudent to do so."
Elections are set for May 1 and the Conservatives lag badly in the polls although the latest releases suggest the gap may be narrowing.
